A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from RADIO Amplified to RADIOv2.5. The main text, equations, tables and appendices support reliable comparison. V1's oversized Figure A1 is clipped on the page, but its complete embedded image is recoverable.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training experiments, classification, segmentation, 3D and VLM evaluations, and extensive ablations and appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds a block-wise versus output token-merging comparison in Appendix A.1.4, Table A4.

M1.justification: The backbone, teachers, multi-resolution training, mosaic augmentation, PHI-S and token-compression procedure are retained. V2 explicitly explains output-only merging and evaluates a block-wise alternative; it does not establish a change to the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Training data and classification, segmentation, 3D and VLM task coverage remain unchanged. Pascal VOC and additional dense-task datasets emphasized in v2 were already evaluated in v1, including its appendices. The new merging comparison uses existing VLM benchmarks.

E2.justification: V2 adds original-style block-wise ToMe as an evaluated comparator to output merging in Table A4. V1 already compared pixel unshuffling and output merging, but lacked this block-wise VLM comparison. Other comparator sets remain unchanged after matching renamed RADIO models.

E3.justification: Table 9 changes the reported resolution of the -g model from 768×768 to 672×672 while retaining its scores; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. New Table A4 compares merging configurations at 768×768 and 196 output tokens, changing merging location, matching features and target partitioning together.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.1.4 tests incremental block-wise merging against one-shot output merging. The existing multi-resolution, teacher-balancing, SAM-inclusion, partitioning, feature-selection and compression analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added comparison continues the existing practice of reporting point estimates and benchmark averages.

E6.justification: New Table A4 reports a block-wise average of 61.76 against the retained output-merging average of 63.19. Figure 1 changes the surface-normal score from 62.50 to 65.50 although Table 1 still gives 62.5. New Section 5.2 claims a 5.9-point merging gain, whereas Table 1's D-to-E results imply approximately 2.79 points. Other benchmark scores are retained.

T1.justification: New Section 2.1 formally defines summary and patch representations, teacher-specific projections, and per-teacher and aggregate distillation losses in Equations 1–6. The existing PHI-S, fidelity and scale-equivariance mathematics remain equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: resolution-robust agglomeration, mosaic augmentation and teacher balancing, visual-token compression, and feature-selection findings. Renaming and added supporting material do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Table 8 newly explains the larger parameter counts through a CPE position-embedding buffer and argues that it adds little computation or representational capacity. Section 6.1 also attributes SAM-CLIP's weaker segmentation to its teacher composition. Existing qualifications about DPT capacity and unequal tiling budgets remain.

D1.justification: Table A4 specifies block-wise merge counts, target allocation and the output-merging stride. V2 also documents CPE buffer dimensions and explains that PHI-S inversion can be folded into the final adaptor projection. Training hyperparameters and code/model access instructions are retained.

R1.justification: V1's brief introductory positioning is expanded into a four-part Related Work section covering agglomeration, multi-resolution models, multi-encoder VLMs and downstream applications. V2 adds substantive comparisons with FlexiViT, NaViT and BRAVE, discusses additional applications, and cites original ToMe for the new comparison.

P1.justification: The exposition is substantially expanded and reorganized through a new knowledge-agglomeration background, dedicated Related Work section, separate benchmark and ablation subsections, and an A–E configuration narrative. The SigLIP subsection moves earlier, and model names and explanatory passages are revised throughout.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table A4, relabels Table 1 configurations, relocates Figures 5–7 and redraws several PCA comparisons. Figure 3 becomes a smaller single-column display, Figure 4's caption is corrected, and Appendix Figure A1 replaces the overflowing montage with four fully visible examples and its caption. Most table structures and the overall format remain intact.

improvement.justification: The expanded formulation and research positioning make v2 easier to assess, Table A4 adds useful evidence for the practical merging choice, and Figure A1's layout problem is resolved. These provide a limited net improvement. New reporting inconsistencies—the Figure 1/Table 1 disagreement and unsupported 5.9-point summary—reduce numerical reliability and limit the gains.
